citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bernstein, M. S., and Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei (Stanford University, Dresden University of Technology, Yahoo Inc., Snapchat Inc.)
description: Visual Genome is a large-scale dataset of 108,249 images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. Each image contains an average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 pairwise relationships, and 17 QA pairs. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases are canonicalized to WordNet synsets, enabling structured knowledge representation for cognitive computer vision tasks.
name: Visual Genome
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 QA pairs. Verification used 3 unique workers per annotation with majority voting (2 out of 3 required for acceptance).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Geographic distribution: United States 93.02%, Philippines 1.29%, Kenya 1.13%, India 0.94%, Russia 0.50%, Canada 0.47%, Others 2.65%. Age range: 18 to 68 years old, majority between 25 and 34 years old. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Canonicalization precision and recall were evaluated on held-out test sets of 200 randomly sampled items: Objects: 88.0% precision, 98.5% recall; Attributes: 85.7% precision, 95.9% recall; Relationships: 92.9% precision, 88.5% recall. The dataset achieved a 94.1% worker retention rate. Noun phrase extraction from region descriptions achieved 99% recall on a manually annotated subset of 200 descriptions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multiple staged annotation pipeline: (1) Region descriptions: workers drew 3 bounding boxes and wrote 3 descriptions per image; subsequent workers added descriptions not yet written (enforced via BLEU score threshold of 0.7), until 50 descriptions per image were collected. (2) Object extraction: workers extracted objects from descriptions and drew tight bounding boxes satisfying coverage and quality requirements. (3) Attributes/relationships/region graphs: workers added attributes to objects and connected object pairs with relationships based on region descriptions. (4) Scene graphs: region graphs merged by combining co-referenced objects (IoU ≥ 0.8). (5) QA pairs: freeform QAs (8 pairs per image, at least 3 different W-types) and region-based QAs (for regions >5k pixels and >4 words). All annotations verified via majority voting (3 workers, 2/3 agreement required) or rapid judgments for objects.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as the top synsets include humans playing sports (ski, ballplayer, racket). Certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) are overrepresented due to a bias in the image source (YFCC100M/MS-COCO). 93.02% of crowd workers contributed from the United States, which may introduce cultural and linguistic biases in annotations. The dataset was designed without bias toward a particular task, unlike previous datasets collected for single tasks like image classification.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected entirely through Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) crowdsourcing. Over 33,000 unique workers contributed approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs). The dataset was collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Images were sourced from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO (108,249 images). Workers were paid $6-$8 per hour. The pipeline involved multiple stages: region descriptions, object extraction with bounding boxes, attribute/relationship extraction, scene graph construction, and QA pair collection, each with verification steps.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M (Yahoo Flickr Creative Commons 100M) and MS-COCO datasets. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users, ranging from 72 pixels to 1280 pixels wide with an average width of 500 pixels.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 6 months of data collection after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, User-generated content data
rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. Relationship canonicalization achieved only 77.6% mapping accuracy. The dataset is biased towards images of people and certain sports. Worker annotations may contain subjective, vague, or opinionated descriptions that were filtered during verification. The dataset covers 972 WordNet synsets for images, which may not represent all visual concepts equally.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Scene graphs were constructed by merging region graph nodes corresponding to the same object using an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.8 for bounding box overlap, with worker confirmation for merges. For the QA experiment, data was split 60% training and 40% test. For attribute/relationship experiments, 80% training, 10% validation, 10% test splits were used, with random sampling of 500 instances per attribute category to balance class sizes.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases were canonicalized to WordNet synsets using Stanford NLP tools for noun phrase extraction, mapped to most frequent matching synsets by WordNet lexeme counts, with hand-crafted rules for the 30 most common failure cases for objects, 15 rules for attributes, and 20 rules for relationships. Attributes were normalized by morphological stemming. Relationships were mapped using WordNet sentence frames and root hypernyms. All mappings were verified by AMT workers who chose among 5 synset options. Region descriptions were preprocessed by removing non-alphanumeric characters, lowercasing, and stripping excess whitespace. BLEU score thresholds (0.7) were used to enforce diversity in region descriptions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Visual Genome aims to enable cognitive computer vision tasks such as image description and question answering, which could enable important applications including image search, question answering systems, and robotic interactions. The dataset is intended to advance comprehensive scene understanding in AI systems.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for: image description/captioning (dense and region-based), visual question answering, object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction/extraction, scene graph generation, semantic image retrieval, image understanding evaluation, knowledge base construction, action recognition, and spatial orientation understanding between objects.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) / Stanford CoreNLP NLP toolkit used to automatically extract nouns from region descriptions as suggestions for workers during object extraction, and to extract noun phrases for canonicalization. BLEU score (Papineni et al., 2002) used programmatically to enforce diversity in region descriptions. word2vec (Mikolov et al., 2013) used for semantic analysis of descriptions. WordNet (Miller, 1995) used for canonicalization of all concepts.
